I am 52 and I went to school for a few years, enough to read the cooperative receipt and do rough sums in my head. This 0.57-hectare plot is my own land and it is the plot I rely on most, so I put my inputs here first. Last season I applied one bag of DAP and half a bag of urea on this piece and the yield was clearly better than the unfertilized corner of my farm, so I will do the same this year — that comes to about 35 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare, which is what my cash allows after I paid school fees for my children. I will also spread two oxcart loads of manure from my cattle pen because I want to keep this soil dark and soft since it belongs to me. I will plant my own saved seed; I have not seen the improved type grow well enough on my neighbor's plot to risk the extra price. No spraying and no irrigation — we depend on the belg and meher rains in this area. My wife, my eldest son, and I will work this plot from ploughing to harvest, about 45 family days in total. It is small enough that we can manage it ourselves, so I will not hire any outside labor.
